Notarial Law

Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

← Back to search
About this programme

UCR currently cannot construct a sufficiently close programme for a meaningful curriculum comparison.

VU Notarial Law develops legal analysis and preventive advice about property, family, inheritance and business relationships. Students build a broad legal foundation before advanced Dutch private and tax law, notarial practice, pleading and an independent legal thesis.

UCR offers valuable study of comparative law, private law, European and international law, business and negotiation. These courses do not form a complete programme with the Dutch notarial, property, inheritance, family and tax-law depth that defines this degree. We therefore show the verified VU curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a comparable alternative.

Academic year: 2026–2027

All 180 EC are compulsory. This plan follows the revised later-year curriculum for students entering in 2026. There is no minor space. Professional identity and Dutch language testing are integrated credit or grade requirements. Thesis entry requires 120 EC including Legal Skills; pleading requires 99 EC including Legal Skills. Course prerequisites and attendance rules apply. Further study and professional training are required for notarial qualification.
